notes: T591 (watch-fleet times + model fixes) — three small improvements to untracked/watch-fleet.sh, acceptance met, test-first per the standing tooling rule. FIX 1 — times column: every row type now carries an HH:MM at the SAME column as PROGRESS's elapsed column (cols 23-28; digits 23-27). CONCERNS shows FIRST-SEEN time, persisted in /tmp/weizigo/fleet-concerns.tsv (env-overridable via FLEET_CONC_STATE; survives fleet restarts; a concern that clears and reappears gets a fresh first-seen; shared across concurrent fleet instances). RECENT shows the lane trailer.log's mtime (last kill/resolve). DONE shows the store `done` field converted UTC->local (matches the header and RECENT mtimes; timezone choice noted in the script header). FIX 2 — RECENT window narrowed 3 days -> 24 h (`-mtime -1`), so HH:MM is unambiguous within a day. FIX 3 — PROGRESS model extraction now falls back from `--model X` to the --dsflash/--dspro subagent startup aliases (new mflag() helper; a lane's argv during startup is `bin/subagent ... --dsflash T<id>` with no --model, which previously rendered an empty model column until the runner spawned). TEST-FIRST: new arm H in tools/regression-watch-fleet.sh (wired into zig build test via the existing watch_fleet_regression step) — scratch git-init'd repo + scratch store + scratch FLEET_CONC_STATE, seeded in_progress/done tasks, a --dsflash alias worker, a fresh and a >24 h-old fake bakeoff lane. Shown RED against the pre-fix live file (empty model column, no times, old-lane not aged out), GREEN after. arm H also pins the first-seen to a known epoch and asserts the row shows 00:00 (proving persistence, not per-frame freshness), and asserts the times token lands at PROGRESS's elapsed column in every section. ACCEPTANCE verified in a real one-shot run: CONCERNS `T568 L1 console 14:14 ...`, DONE rows with 14:13/14:12/... completed times, and a live --dspro worker rendered `T591 dspro 0'01 00.00 ...` in PROGRESS; RECENT 24 h window proven by arm H's old-lane absence. SURPRISE (for the T466/T492 owner, NOT fixed here): the documented arm F/G red (`RED script tools/regression-watch-fleet.sh` in docs/infra/suite-truth.md, 'the live file does not surface the T492-bundle-path worker') has a different root cause than recorded — macOS `sh` is bash in POSIX mode, where `VAR=1 . file` (special builtin) EXPORTS the assignment; arm E's `WATCH_FLEET_SOURCE=1 . "$LIVE"` (and arm A's) therefore leaks WATCH_FLEET_SOURCE=1 into the environment, and every later `sh "$LIVE_COPY"` (arms F/G) exits at the live file's source-guard with an EMPTY frame — the T492 worker never gets a chance to render. Evidence: running the regression under `bash` (non-POSIX) shows T492 rendered and arm G green, with arm F failing only on the T991-hidden expectation (a genuine behavior mismatch: the live file shows workers whose argv contains watch-fleet.sh; only the script's own $0 invocation is skipped). Fixing F/G belongs to that territory (would also require re-running the suite-truth ratchet gate); arm H is made immune via `env -u WATCH_FLEET_SOURCE` on its frame. Also noted: managent's findRepoRoot hard-exits (exit 1) when its cwd has no .git up the tree even when MANAGENT_STORE is set — scratch repos in regressions that touch the store must `git init` (arm H does; arms F/G never touch the store so never hit it). No claim-status changes proposed; no live store writes (scratch stores only).
